genius.notes: Coinbase, Inc. remains the issuerEntity, supported by Flipcash terms; the brand partner does not mint or redeem USDF. Coinbase publicly permits 1:1 USDF/USDC conversions, supporting redemptionPolicyPresent, with no independent monthly USDF reserve attestation located. NYDFS lists Coinbase, Inc. with virtual currency and money transmitter licenses separately from Coinbase Custody Trust Company, LLC. OCC Corporate Decision 1370 grants preliminary conditional charter approval to proposed Coinbase National Trust Company and expressly says the proposed bank does not plan to issue stablecoins. That separate entity is not assigned as the USDF issuer or treated as GENIUS approval. Coinbase excludes Custom Stablecoins from its EEA, New York and Canada platform customers. Federal issuer frameworks remain proposed on the reviewed October 7 record; Treasury expects January 18, 2027 effectiveness and a July 18, 2028 general DASP offer-sale deadline.

negativeEvidenceReview.summary: As of 2026-10-07, no public GENIUS PPSI approval, state qualification or named official pending application was located for Coinbase, Inc. as USDF issuer in the checked regulator materials and targeted searches. The reviewed federal documents describe proposed issuer frameworks; Treasury's September 30 interim final rule concerns state certification procedures and states that certifications await PRA approval. Ordinary licenses and reserve disclosures do not establish PPSI approval. No token-specific GENIUS warning or prohibition was located. This is a bounded public-evidence finding, not proof about nonpublic filings.

applicabilityBasis.summary: USDF is Coinbase-issued, USD-referenced digital cash used for Flipcash payments and settlement. Coinbase discloses 1:1 USDC custody backing and conversion to USDC; Flipcash terms identify Coinbase, Inc. as sole issuer and reserve/redemption operator. The apparent payment-stablecoin classification reflects these payment and stable-value characteristics; public conversion documentation promises USDC rather than an unconditional direct dollar redemption.
